Title: January 22, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting
Overview: The January 22, 2026 special meeting covered the consent agenda, a purchasing code update, community change requests for the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan, a proposed metro district policy framework, and a regional homelessness appointment, along with a Holocaust Remembrance Day declaration. Council unanimously passed consent items 3A through 3G, adopted Ordinance 8731 to modernize the city's purchasing procedures, and approved an amended list of comprehensive plan change requests that removed a Sue Drive request and added wildfire mitigation and agricultural water use requests. No final action was taken on the metro district framework, which staff will bring back in April with a regulating ordinance, and the regional homelessness working group appointment was deferred to a later consent item, with Tina volunteering as alternate.

Topic1.Title: Opening, announcements, and roll call
Topic1.Summary: The meeting was called to order with an announcement about 2026 boards and commissions recruitment, which is open until January 25th. Council took roll call and confirmed a quorum was present.

Topic2.Title: International Holocaust Remembrance Day declaration
Topic2.Summary: Mayor Pro Tem Winer read a declaration recognizing January 27th, 2026 as International Holocaust Remembrance Day. The declaration condemns antisemitism, hatred, and bigotry and pledges solidarity with the Jewish community.

Topic3.Title: Consent agenda items 3A through 3G
Topic3.Summary: Council discussed the consent agenda, including a letter to Xcel Energy regarding expectations after the city declined an offer in 2025. Council praised staff's draft and then passed items 3A through 3G unanimously.

Topic4.Title: Ordinance 8731 purchasing procedures update
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented updates to the city's purchasing code, the first since 1997, including raising the informal bid threshold from $50,000 to $100,000, allowing alternative construction delivery methods, and creating a business opportunity program. Council asked about support for small, minority, and women-owned businesses and about environmental sustainability language. Ordinance 8731 was adopted unanimously after a public comment period.

Topic5.Title: Community change requests for the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update
Topic5.Summary: Staff screened 34 community change requests for the comprehensive plan update and recommended which should advance for further analysis. Council removed request 10 on the south side of Sue Drive after residents raised concerns about lack of outreach and neighborhood impacts, and added back requests 26 and 27 on wildfire mitigation and agricultural water use. Council approved the amended list unanimously.

Topic6.Title: Metro district policy framework
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented a policy framework for regulating commercial-focused metropolitan districts, covering development type, mill levy caps, operations and maintenance, fees and revenue bonds, privately placed debt, and amendment oversight. Council asked questions about governance, oversight, and competitiveness and generally supported the approach. Staff plans to return in April with a regulating ordinance and model service plan.

Topic7.Title: Regional homelessness working group appointment
Topic7.Summary: Council discussed filling a vacancy on the Boulder County Elected Officials Regional Working Group on Homelessness, previously held by Lauren Folkart. Council members Matt and Mark were asked to resolve who would volunteer, with Tina volunteering as alternate, and the appointment will be handled later on consent.
